Attached is the updated capacity proposal (orion_capacity_proposal_v2.pdf) with the sizing we discussed: 8 p100-equivalent GPUs for inference (1.6M tokens/day baseline, 2x peak burst) and a 2-node KV cache cluster. - Confirm average prompt + response token lengths and % of embedding calls vs. generation.
- Is July 10 a hard go-live for production? We can aim for a July 10 window but need to finalize reservation and provisioning plan by July 2.

If those look right I’ll circulate a proposed reservation commitment and a short mutual action plan.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt

- Karthik: be prepared to escalate pricing/SLA trade-offs to leadership if we recommend prioritizing Orion.

We need a decision and messaging to Orion and Nimbus by EOD July 7.

Thanks — Hannah

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-07-03T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated capacity — initial sizing and timeline

Quick summary from capacity planning after reviewing Orion and Nimbus commitments:

Scenario A — Prioritize Orion (recommended):
- Reserve 8 GPU equivalents in Pool A for Orion from July 8–30.
- Nimbus keeps existing baseline but any extra burst requests routed to Pool B (if available) or throttled to a soft-fail with automatic fallback to smaller model variant.
- Impact: Orion gets green-field run for initial launch; Nimbus experiences up to 25% reduced burst headroom for two weeks. Estimated ARR risk: low for Nimbus (they have flexible SLAs), high uplift for Orion (they sign full-year commitment on close).

Scenario B — Strict first-come-first-served (fair-share):
- Keep both in Pool A; implement dynamic fairness with weighted tokens based on committed throughput.
- Impact: Both customers get partial burst guarantees; higher risk of latency spikes during cross-customer peaks. No single customer blocked, but user experience could degrade.

Recommendation: Scenario A. Commercially, Orion is ready to sign a larger committed reservation (deal_id ORC-2026-1475) and July 10 is a hard deadline; Nimbus can accept staged throttles short-term. Ops work for Pool reassignments: ~6 hours automation + manual routing steps.

I attached a short sim (internal) — allocation_matrix_q3.xlsx — with expected token-level KPIs. If we go A, ops should start provisioning July 5.

- Dylan
Principal Planner, Capacity

David / Sara — quick update and decision after internal coordination. We will prioritize Orion Cloud for the July 8–30 reservation window. Operational notes:

- Reserved capacity: 8 GPU equivalents in Pool A (provisioning starts July 5).
- Fallbacks: If simultaneous peak with Nimbus occurs, requests will failover to a smaller model variant (pre-agreed) and we’ll enable short-term throttles on Nimbus.
- SLA: We’ll include a one-time SLA exception for the July 8–30 reservation in the SOW; legal has prepared an addendum and procurement should see the DocuSign link below.

Next steps for Orion:
- Sara: please sign the addendum in DocuSign (https://docusign.net/link/Orion-Commit-ORC-2026-1475) by July 18 to lock the reservation.
- David: ops kickoff call on July 6 at 10:00 PT to confirm routing details and test KV cache warming.

Karthik / Dylan / Jordan: please coordinate provisioning and notify Nimbus account lead with the mitigation plan (I’ll draft the outbound note).

Thanks everyone — excited to get Orion live.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
